claims.text: The official Node.js Release Working Group schedule lists current release-line status and phase dates; its published dates are explicitly subject to change. As retrieved for the target date, it lists 22.x as Maintenance LTS, 24.x as Active LTS, and 26.x as Current.

evidence.locator: Release schedule and dates-subject-to-change note, lines 191-204

claims.text: Node 24 (Krypton) entered Active LTS on 2025-10-28, is scheduled to enter Maintenance on 2026-10-20, and has scheduled end-of-life on 2028-04-30. These are schedule dates, not a guarantee against later schedule changes.

Node 26 is scheduled to enter LTS on 2026-10-28. As of 2026-10-17 it is not LTS: the schedule calls it Current, and the official release page also labels v26 Current. The scheduled date is subject to change.

evidence.locator: Release phases and v26 marked Current, lines 39-52

claims.text: Node 22 (Jod) is in Maintenance LTS, not Active LTS, as of 2026-10-17; its scheduled end-of-life is 2027-04-30. The official versions page independently identifies v22 as LTS and lists its latest update as 2026-09-23.

evidence.locator: v22 status and last-updated date, line 54

claims.text: For a deployment that requires LTS immediately on 2026-10-17, choose Node 24: it is already Active LTS, whereas Node 26 remains Current until its scheduled LTS transition on 2026-10-28. Node's official guidance says production applications should use Active LTS or Maintenance LTS releases.

evidence.locator: 24.x Active LTS and 26.x Current statuses, lines 194-199
Production guidance and v26/v24 statuses, lines 39-52

claims.text: The release schedule defines release-line phases and dates; it does not establish the exact Node patch installed in any particular deployment or prove that the deployment is receiving security fixes. As an as-of-date reference, the official release blog lists Node 24.22.0 (LTS) and Node 26.12.0 (Current), both posted 2026-10-14. Verify the deployed binary/package version and its source separately, and keep it updated; the schedule itself is not an installed-patch or security guarantee.

evidence.locator: Latest release entries and publication dates, lines 19-33
Release phases, supported release lines, and schedule caveat, lines 199-210

recommendation: For a deployment that needs LTS as of 2026-10-17, deploy the latest verified Node 24 LTS patch that is compatible with the application; the official release blog shows 24.22.0 (LTS) posted on 2026-10-14. Reassess Node 26 after its scheduled 2026-10-28 LTS transition, confirming its actual status and current patch then. Node 22 remains supported as Maintenance LTS through its scheduled 2027-04-30 EOL, but is in its maintenance phase.
unknowns: Official schedules explicitly say dates can change; no independently archived schedule snapshot exactly at 2026-10-17 was retrieved, so the as-of status is cross-checked against the official versions page and release posts available for that date.
No target deployment, host package database, container image, or runtime was inspected. Its installed Node version, vendor patch/backport policy, and actual security state are therefore unknown.
LTS status indicates the upstream support phase, not that a particular downstream distribution or application image has installed the newest upstream patch.
